author: Rahul kp
title: Joint Products
hook: split the joint cost by value!
simple_words: One process gives many products. Share the joint cost in the ratio of what each product can earn after further costs.

definitions.meaning: Two or more main products of equal importance, produced together from the same raw material and process, and separated at the split-off point.
Final sales value less further processing cost after split-off, less selling and distribution cost, if any.

key_points: Joint cost is common up to the ==split-off point==; it cannot be traced to one product.
==NRV method== apportions joint cost in the ratio of NRV of each product.
It is used when products need further processing after split-off.
!!Only the further cost after split-off is deducted; joint cost is never deducted from sales value!!.
formula_hook: sales less later costs, then share

formulas.name: NRV of a product
formulas.legend: S = final sales value of the product, F = further processing cost after split-off, SD = selling and distribution cost, if any.

formulas.name: Joint cost share of a product
formulas.numerator: NRV of the product × Total joint cost
formulas.denominator: Total NRV of all joint products
formulas.legend: Numerator uses the NRV of that one product; denominator is the sum of NRV of all joint products.

insight.text: Higher NRV means a bigger share of joint cost, because that product can bear more of it.

memory_trick.explanation: Sell value first, Subtract later costs to get NRV, then Split the joint cost in the NRV ratio.

steps: Write final sales value of each
Split joint cost in that ratio
exam_tip: Check whether the question gives sales value at split-off or after further processing. Use the NRV method only for the second case.

doubt.question: Why not split joint cost by units produced?
doubt.answer: Units ignore value. A low-value product would carry too much cost. NRV matches cost to ability to bear it.

mistakes.wrong: Deducting the joint cost from sales value to get NRV
mistakes.right: Deduct only further processing and selling costs after split-off. Then apportion the joint cost on NRV.

mistakes.wrong: Ignoring further processing cost of a product
mistakes.right: Deduct each product's own further processing cost before finding the NRV ratio.

mistakes.wrong: Adding further cost to the share of joint cost, then dividing again
mistakes.right: Joint cost share comes from the NRV ratio. Add the product's further cost afterwards only for its total cost.

check_notes: Writer: No past-paper list was given. Check the "Mistakes" wording against ICMAI study material.

Checker 1: Definition 2 / Formula 1 legend: the ICMAI study material describes the NRV method as sales value at the finished stage less estimated profit margin (if given), selling and distribution expenses and post-split-off costs. The note's formula NRV = S − (F + SD) is the standard working, but it should add: 'less estimated profit margin, if the question gives one'.

Checker 1: Mistake 3 'wrong' wording is unclear: 'Adding further cost to the share of joint cost, then dividing again' does not describe a recognisable slip. Rephrase as 'Adding the further processing cost to the joint cost before apportioning it in the NRV ratio'. The 'right' text is correct.

Checker 1: Exam tip: 'Use the NRV method only for the second case' is slightly too absolute. Better: 'If the sales value at split-off is given, use the sales-value-at-split-off method. If only the final sales value after further processing is given, use the NRV method.'
